title: Mögen und der gern-Trick
summary: Mögen for liking things and the universal gern trick for liking to do things

blocks.title: mögen — für Dinge, die du magst
blocks.body: **mögen** is your verb for liking a *thing*: *Ich mag Käse* (I like cheese). It conjugates a little irregularly: **ich mag, du magst, er/sie/es mag, wir mögen, ihr mögt, sie/Sie mögen**. Negate it the normal noun way, with **kein**: *Ich mag keinen Fisch.*

blocks.title: Der gern-Trick
blocks.body: Want to say you like *doing* something? Don't reach for a new verb — just add **gern** (gladly) right after any verb. *Ich esse gern Pizza* literally says "I eat gladly pizza", but it means **I like eating pizza**. It's the single most useful word in this whole module.
blocks.callout: One new thing: **gern** turns any verb into "I like to …".

blocks.title: mögen (ein Ding) vs Verb + gern (eine Handlung)

pairs.left: Ich mag Kaffee. — I like coffee (the thing)
pairs.right: Ich trinke gern Kaffee. — I like drinking coffee (the action)
pairs.note: Same idea, two grammar tools: mögen for nouns, verb + gern for actions.

blocks.prompt: How do you say 'I like reading'?
blocks.explain: *Ich lese gern.* — the verb *lesen* conjugated, plus *gern* right after. *Ich mag lesen* sounds foreign to a German ear.

blocks.hint: mögen + object, no article needed for a general statement.
blocks.explain: *Ich mag Käse.* — general likes about food usually drop the article, just like in English.

blocks.title: Bau deinen gern-Satz
blocks.prompt: Build a sentence using the gern trick.
Write three sentences about food and drink you like — mix mögen and the gern trick.
